*tuatara-normal-cursor-shape*nilnil, :block, :bar, :underlineThe cursor's shape in NORMAL state.
*tuatara-normal-tab-modes*(org-mode)a list, each a major mode's nameThe major modes where M-x tuatara-normal-tab in NORMAL state does what TAB does in the mode, the modes derived from them too.
*tuatara-support-cursor-colour*nila colour name such as :red, a number 0-255 or "#rrggbb", or nilThe cursor's colour in support buffers.
*tuatara-support-cursor-shape*nilnil, :block, :bar, :underlineThe cursor's shape in support buffers (lists, help, Messages).
*tui-colours*:auto:auto, :24-bit, 256, 16, 8, nilHow many colours Tuatara uses in a terminal.
*tui-mouse*tt, nilWhether the mouse works in Tuatara in a terminal as in its window.
*tui-padding*0a whole number, 0 or more, or a list, each a whole number, 0 or moreThe room, in whole cells, between the edges of the terminal and Tuatara's text.
*tui-pictures*:auto:auto, t, nilWhether pictures (a preview of an image, a PDF's pages) are shown in the terminal.
*typing-pause*1/2a number, 0 or moreThe seconds without a key typed before work over a text too large to go through at each key starts.
*undo-limit*nilnil, or a whole number, 1 or moreThe most memory, in octets, the undo history of one buffer may hold.
*use-system-clipboard*tt, nilWhether what is killed or copied goes on the system clipboard as well.
*user-full-name*nilnil, or textYour full name, as "Ann Taranaki": the author of an exported document with no #+author:, %author% in a note template and $AUTHOR in a snippet.
*visual-line-modes*nila list, each (MODE . VALUE)Major modes whose buffers mark the fill column with a line down the window, or not: a list of (MODE .
*window-colours-from-desktop*nilt, nilWhether the window paints text and ground the theme leaves without a colour in the colours of the desktop's GTK theme.
*window-min-height*4a whole number, 1 or moreThe fewest rows, its mode line included, a window may be left with when it is split or made smaller.
*window-min-width*10a whole number, 1 or moreThe fewest columns a window may be left with when it is split or made narrower.
*wipe-passes*1a whole number, 1 or moreHow many times a file wiped is overwritten with random octets before it is deleted.
*word-completion-keep-case*tt, nilWhether word completion finds words whatever the case typed, and keeps the case typed: with "foo" typed, a word Foobar is put in as foobar, and with "FOO" typed, it is put in as FOOBAR.

Every command

The name, keys and purpose of every command Tuatara has.

The earlier chapters describe the commands of each subject where you meet them. This chapter lists them all in one table, in the alphabetical order of their names, so that you can look one up by name. The table is made from the program each time this manual is made, so it never lists a command that Tuatara does not have.

The table has four columns. The first two are keys, as chapter 1 explains: the modal keys, which work only with modal editing on, and the non-modal keys, which work with it off too. Each shows up to three keys, the shortest first, or "none". A command with no key at all says M-x and its name in the second column, because you can only run it by its name. The third column is the name of the command and the fourth says what it does, in one sentence. The keys of a command can differ from one major mode to another, and the table shows keys from every mode. A key written C-x means hold down Control and press x.

To run a command by its name, press M-x, type a few letters of the name and press RET. To find a command from within the editor, press C-h f and type a few letters of its name. Tuatara shows its keys and its full description. To find the command that a key runs, press C-h k and then the key. To find the commands that mention a word, press C-h a and type the word.

nonen, C-c nlist-next-entryGo to the next entry of the list, the start of its first line, passing over the headings of its sections.
nonep, C-c plist-previous-entryGo to the entry of the list before the one on the current line, the start of its first line, passing over the headings of its sections.
noneS-TABlist-toggle-all-foldsFold every section of the list, or unfold them all when every one is folded; a section not in the list now keeps its fold for when it comes back.
noneTABlist-toggle-foldFold the section of the list the current line is in, its heading left showing, or unfold it when it is folded.
noneC-x / tlist-toggle-headerTake the first line of a file of records as its header, or as a record like the rest; the same again switches back; with a count, a header when it is positive, a record when it is zero or less.
noneC-x / Llist-toggle-header-lockKeep the first line of a file of records, its header, at the top of the window as the rest scrolls under it, coloured as it is below; the same again lets it scroll away; with a count, kept when it is positive, let go when it is zero or less.
nonetlist-toggle-marksMark the entries the list shows that are not marked and take the mark off those marked; those marked for deletion (D), or given a mark of another kind, stay so, as do the entries a filter or a folded section hides.
noneP, C-c Plist-toggle-previewTurn the preview beside this list on or off: the entry on the current line shown in a window beside the list, on its right when there is room, else below it, following the cursor from line to line.
noneU, C-c Ulist-unmark-allTake every mark off the entries of the list, of any kind; in rimu, those of the files marked in other directories too.
noneu, C-c ulist-unmark-entryTake the mark off the entry on the current line of the list, of any kind, and move down; with a count, off as many entries, up the list for a negative one.
nonel, RET, C-c llist-visitOpen the entry on the current line of the list: the buffer, the bookmark's place, the file; on a section's heading, fold or unfold the section.
noneo, C-c olist-visit-otherOpen the entry on the current line of the list in another window; on a section's heading, fold or unfold the section.
noneC-M-rliteral-search-backwardSearch backward as you type for literal text; see literal-search-forward.
noneC-M-sliteral-search-forwardSearch forward as you type for literal text: keys as in regex-search-forward, nothing typed special.
noneM-x load-themeload-themeChoose a colour theme, with each theme's description beside it.
noneC-c LlspStart the language servers of the current buffer's language for its project, after asking whether you trust the project: a server runs the project's code (build scripts, macros, plugins).
noneC-c alsp-code-actionsOffer the language server's fixes and changes for the selection, or for point: those for what it found wrong there first; the one chosen is made.
noneC-c klsp-code-lensRun what a language server says of the current line (a code lens: Run test, 3 references), chosen when there are several, as the server's own command.
noneC-c Klsp-code-lenses-modeShow what language servers say of lines (3 references, Run test) faint at each line's end, or no longer; M-x lsp-code-lens runs one.
noneC-c hlsp-describe-thing-at-pointShow what the language server knows of the thing at point (its type, its documentation) in Help.
noneC-c llsp-diagnosticsList what the language servers found wrong in the open files, a line each, then in the files of their projects not open, in a window across the bottom; RET there goes to it, opening the file.
noneM-x lsp-eventslsp-eventsList the last messages to and from the language servers the current buffer is open in (all those running when it is in none), the newest last, and what each said on its error output: to see what a server was asked and answered when it does not do what it should; the last 500 of each are kept.
noneC-c Ilsp-find-implementationsGo to the implementations of the thing at point (of a trait, an interface, an abstract method), as its language server finds them: there at once when it is one, else listed in xref.
noneC-c rlsp-find-referencesList where the thing at point is used, as its language server finds it, in xref: RET goes to one.
noneC-c glsp-find-symbolGo to a function, type or other name of the current buffer's project, as its language server finds them by what you type (the name at point offered): each is listed with what it is and where, and the one chosen is gone to.
noneC-c Tlsp-find-type-definitionGo to the definition of the type of the thing at point (a variable's type, a function's result), as its language server finds it.
noneC-c zlsp-foldHide the lines of the block the cursor is in (a function's body, a struct, a run of imports), as its language server knows them, under the block's first line; on a line whose block is hidden, show it again.
noneC-c Zlsp-fold-allHide every outermost block of the file, as its language server knows them, under its first line; with any hidden, show all again.
noneM-x lsp-forget-projectlsp-forget-projectTrust the current buffer's project no more: its language servers end, and no longer start by themselves.
noneC-c clsp-incoming-callsList the places that call the function at point, as its language server knows them, in xref: RET goes to one.
noneC-c ilsp-inlay-hints-modeShow the language servers' inlay hints within the code, or no longer: the types of bindings, the names of the parameters arguments go to.
noneC-c nlsp-next-diagnosticGo to the next place the language servers found something wrong, and say what.
noneC-c olsp-organise-importsHave the language server put the file's imports in order, as its own action for that does it (unused ones taken out, where it does that), once it answers, when the file is still as it was asked of.
noneC-c Clsp-outgoing-callsList the functions the function at point calls, as its language server knows them, in xref: RET goes to one.
noneC-c plsp-previous-diagnosticGo to the place before point where the language servers found something wrong, and say what.
noneC-c Rlsp-renameRename the thing at point everywhere the language server knows it is used, the new name asked for: each file's changes one change undo takes back, nothing saved (C-x s saves them).
noneM-x lsp-restartlsp-restartEnd the language servers the current buffer is open in and start them again; in a project not trusted, none is started (M-x lsp asks first).
noneC-c Slsp-semantic-tokens-modeColour code as its language server sees it, or no longer: each name in the face of its kind (a parameter, a field, a macro), over the mode's colours.
noneM-x lsp-shutdownlsp-shutdownEnd the language servers the current buffer is open in; M-x lsp starts them again.
noneC-x 5 2make-frameOpen another frame showing the current buffer and work in it: a window of its own on the desktop, or in a terminal a whole screen of its own shown in place of the one before, the frames taking turns on the terminal, the mode line naming the one shown (F1, F2).
noneM-x manmanShow a manual page in a buffer of its own, read-only: ask for it by name (ls), with its section (ls(1)) or by section and name (1 ls), completing on the names of the pages the system has.
noneh, C-c hman-backShow the page a link was followed from; close the window when this page was not reached by a link.
nonen, C-c nman-next-sectionGo to the start of the next section heading of the manual page.
nonep, C-c pman-previous-sectionGo to the start of the section heading before the line point is on.
noneM-x mark-defunmark-defunSelect the definition point is in, or the one after: point at its start, with the comments right above it and the blank lines above those, and the mark after it.
noneM-x mark-end-of-sentencemark-end-of-sentenceSet the mark at the end of the sentence, point staying, and activate the region; with a count, that many sentences.
noneM-hmark-paragraphSelect the paragraph at point: point at the blank line before it (or the start of the text), the mark at the blank line after it.
noneM-x mark-run-adoptmark-run-adoptTake the selection into a mark run: its keys then grow it from where it is.
noneM-x mark-run-buffer-endmark-run-buffer-endStretch the run's end on to the end of the text, or with no run go there.
noneM-x mark-run-buffer-startmark-run-buffer-startStretch the run's start back to the start of the text, or with no run go there.
noneM-x mark-run-cancelmark-run-cancelDrop the selection and end the mark run.
noneM-x mark-run-downmark-run-downMove point down a line, or the count's, without ending the mark run.
noneM-x mark-run-exchangemark-run-exchangeSwap point and the mark, so that h j k l adjust the run's other end.
noneM-x mark-run-leftmark-run-leftMove point back a character, or the count's, without ending the mark run.
noneM-x mark-run-line-backwardmark-run-line-backwardSelect the line point is on, or grow the run's start up by whole lines: a run starting mid-line first takes the start of that line.
noneM-x mark-run-line-endmark-run-line-endStretch the run's end on to the end of its line, or with no run go there.
noneM-x mark-run-line-forwardmark-run-line-forwardSelect the line point is on, its line end included, or grow the run's end down by whole lines: a run ending mid-line first takes the rest of that line.
noneM-x mark-run-line-startmark-run-line-startStretch the run's start back to the start of its line, or with no run go there.
noneM-x mark-run-rightmark-run-rightMove point forward a character, or the count's, without ending the mark run.
noneM-x mark-run-step-backmark-run-step-backPut the mark run back where its last press found it; U puts it forward again.
noneM-x mark-run-step-forwardmark-run-step-forwardPut the mark run forward where u stepped it back from.
MC-z Mmark-run-toggleStart a mark run: the m prefix held down.
noneM-x mark-run-upmark-run-upMove point up a line, or the count's, without ending the mark run.
noneC-M-@, C-M-SPCmark-sexpSet the mark after the next balanced expression, point staying, and activate it; with a count, that many expressions, or before point when negative.
noneC-x hmark-whole-bufferSelect the whole buffer: mark at the end, point at the start; where point was goes on the mark ring, with the mark before.
noneM-@mark-wordSet the mark at the end of the next word, point staying, and activate the region; with a count, that many words.
noneC-c C-omarkdown-follow-link-at-pointFollow the Markdown link point is on (C-c C-o, and RET in NORMAL state): to the heading a table of contents's link (#an-anchor) leads to, a web or mail address in the desktop's program after asking, or a file, visited.
noneM-x match-denote-files-linkmatch-denote-files-linkInsert a link to your files with formatted names whose names match what is asked for, the files it matches listed as it is typed, as a denote: link, which other programs reading those links follow too, written LABEL; in Markdown [LABEL](denote:query-filenames:TEXT) and in text files <denote:query-filenames:TEXT>.
noneC-x n lmatch-formatted-files-linkInsert a link to your files with formatted names whose names match a regular expression, asked for, the files it matches listed as it is typed: LABEL.
noneM-x menu-describemenu-describeList in Help every entry of the open menu: its keys, what it says and the command or argument behind it, those not shown now too.
noneM-x menu-leavemenu-leaveLeave the open menu, asked first when anything in it was changed; it stays open unless the answer is yes.
noneM-x menu-set-optionmenu-set-optionGive the option of the open menu whose key was typed a value, asked for, or take its value away when it has one, or ask it again with that value when the option says so (MENU-ENTRY-REPLACE), or say it is left out of the menu now; the menu stays open.
noneM-x menu-toggle-switchmenu-toggle-switchTurn the switch of the open menu whose key was typed on, or off, or say it is left out of the menu now; the menu stays open.
none<drag-mouse-1>mouse-drag-regionSelect from where the first mouse button went down to where the mouse is now, point following it, in the window it went down in; held above or below that window's text, it scrolls a line at a time.
none<up-mouse-1>mouse-releaseThe first mouse button let go: a drag ends there, what it selected staying selected and becoming the desktop's primary selection, which the middle button pastes in other programs.
none<triple-mouse-1>mouse-select-lineSelect the line the first mouse button went down on three times, its line break too.
none<double-mouse-1>mouse-select-wordSelect the word the first mouse button went down on twice, point at its end: the run of letters, digits and _ there, or of spaces, or of other signs; on a bracket, the bracketed group.
none<down-mouse-1>mouse-set-pointPut point where the first mouse button went down, selecting the window there, and let go of the selection; dragging then selects from there.
noneC-<wheel-up>, C-<wheel-down>mouse-wheel-text-scaleMake the window's font a step larger as the mouse wheel turns up with Ctrl held (C-<wheel-up>), a step smaller as it turns down.
none<mouse-2>mouse-yank-primaryInsert where the middle button was pressed the text selected last in any program (the desktop's primary selection); the mark at its start.
noneM-x name-recorded-keysname-recorded-keysGive the keys recorded last a name, asked for, which then plays them as a command: M-x NAME, or a key bound to it, as C-x e does, a prefix argument as with it.
noneC-x x nnarrow-to-regionShow only the selected text, and keep every command to it: motion, search and replacement, editing and selecting stop at its edges, and the rest of the buffer is out of sight and out of reach until C-x x w.
noneC-x x snarrow-to-sectionShow only the section point is in, and keep every command to it, as C-x x n does for the selection: in Org, the subtree of the headline point is under, the headline with it; in code, the definition point is in (or the one after it), as C-M-a and C-M-e find it.
noneC-x n enew-empty-bufferShow a new empty buffer, untitled (untitled<2> beside one already there), for text that has no file yet: C-x C-s asks where to save it.
noneC-x n nnew-file-formattedMake a new file with a formatted name in FORMATTED-FILE-DIRECTORY: asks what FORMATTED-FILE-PROMPTS says (as standard the title, the subdirectory, the keywords, the kind of file and the template), and names it as find-file-formatted does, with the header for its kind.
noneC-j, RETnewlineInsert a line end at point: a newline, or in a buffer whose lines end with a carriage return and a newline (a Windows file), both; with a count, that many, and none for 0.
jC-n, <down>next-lineMove point down one line (or the prefix argument's worth), keeping the column when possible; where long lines wrap at a word's edge (C-x T l), one row.
noneM-g nnext-placeGo to the next place of the list of places used last: the next line naming a file and line in a compile's output (M-x compile), the next line a search of files found (M-s g), the next place the language servers found something wrong in a buffer, or the next error of LaTeX errors.
noneC-x r Nnumber-rectangle-linesNumber the lines of the rectangle between the mark and point: 1, 2, 3 and on, each with a space after it, put in at the block's left column, a line shorter than that padded out to it; the numbers are right-aligned to the width of the last, and the text of the block moves right to make room.
noneM-x number-rectangle-lines-replacenumber-rectangle-lines-replaceReplace the rectangle between the mark and point with numbers, 1, 2, 3 and on down its lines, nothing after them: to renumber a list, or to turn its bullets into numbers.
noneM-x office-view-pagesoffice-view-pagesShow the pages of the Office document read as text here, in its place.
noneM-x open-dropped-filesopen-dropped-filesVisit the files dropped on the window, in the window they were dropped on, as C-x C-f does, the last one shown; safely, as C-u C-x C-f does, when OPEN-DROPPED-FILES-SAFELY is true.
noneO, C-c Oopen-externallyOpen the file shown, in the desktop's own program for its kind (xdg-open), or the one OPEN-EXTERNALLY-PROGRAMS gives its Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) type, for what Tuatara does not do: printing, forms, playing.
noneC-x n oopen-file-formattedOpen one of your files with formatted names, those in FORMATTED-FILE-DIRECTORY and its subdirectories, choosing among them by any part of the name: listed under their subdirectory or their kind, the ones changed last first, each as its date, its title and its keywords, with its size and when it changed at the right.
noneC-oopen-lineInsert a line end after point, point staying before it; with a count, that many line ends.
noneC-x C-popen-path-at-pointOpen the file or directory whose path is at the cursor in the text, as C-x C-f opens it: a directory (etc, ~/notes/) in a list of it, a file \(~/notes/todo.org, ./README.org, or a file: link's) in its buffer.
noneC-c C-zorg-add-noteAdd a note to the entry point is under (C-c C-z): the note is asked for, and logged where Org logs notes, at the top of its :LOGBOOK: drawer with ORG-LOG-INTO-DRAWER, else after its planning line and properties, in the form - Note taken on [2026-10-01 Thu 18:00] \\ and the note under it.
nonea, C-c a, C-x a aorg-agendaShow the agenda, asking which view: a the agenda of the week (or ORG-AGENDA-SPAN), t the TODO list, m the headlines a match selects (work+urgent-home, TODO="NEXT"), or a view of your own (ORG-AGENDA-CUSTOM-COMMANDS, u the tasks with no tag), or c the entries whose dates look wrong (M-x org-agenda-check-dates), read from ORG-AGENDA-FILES.
nonen, C-c n, C-c C-zorg-agenda-add-noteAdd a note to the entry on the agenda's line, as C-c C-z adds one.
noneC-c C-x Corg-agenda-cancel-taskCancel the task on the agenda's line, as C-c C-x C does in its file: its keyword made CANCELLED and noted with CLOSED:.
noneM-x org-agenda-check-datesorg-agenda-check-datesShow the entries of ORG-AGENDA-FILES whose dates look wrong, each with what is wrong (ORG-ENTRY-DATE-PROBLEM).
noneC, C-c Corg-agenda-clock-cancelCancel the clock, as C-c C-x C-q does, from the agenda: the clock's file saved at once when it is one of ORG-AGENDA-AUTOSAVE-FILES.
noneI, C-c Iorg-agenda-clock-inClock in on the entry on the agenda's line, as M-x org-clock-in does: a clock running is clocked out first.
noneO, C-c Oorg-agenda-clock-outClock out, as C-c C-x C-o does, from the agenda: the clock's file saved at once when it is one of ORG-AGENDA-AUTOSAVE-FILES.
noneD, C-c Dorg-agenda-day-viewShow the agenda of one day: the day at point in the agenda, else today.
noned, C-c d, C-c C-dorg-agenda-deadlineGive the entry on the agenda's line a deadline, the date asked for as C-c C-d asks it; with C-u, take it away.
noneh, C-c horg-agenda-earlierShow the agenda's previous span: the previous week in a week's agenda, the previous day in a day's.
noneTABorg-agenda-gotoShow the entry on the agenda's line in the other window and go there.
nonec, C-c corg-agenda-goto-calendarShow the calendar on the day of the agenda line at point.
noneg horg-agenda-goto-todayShow the agenda's span holding today, point on today's date.
nonel, C-c lorg-agenda-laterShow the agenda's next span: the next week in a week's agenda, the next day in a day's.
noneM-x org-agenda-listorg-agenda-listShow the agenda of this week (or ORG-AGENDA-SPAN): each day with its scheduled tasks, deadlines and timestamps.
noneL, C-c Lorg-agenda-log-modeList what was closed and clocked on each day too, or no longer; ORG-AGENDA-LOG-MODE says how the agenda starts.
nonem, C-c m, C-x a morg-agenda-month-viewShow the agenda of a month: the month of the day at point in the agenda, else this month.
noneg lorg-agenda-previous-viewGo back to the view or span the agenda showed before this one, point on the line it was on, as cd - goes back to the directory before: pressed again, return.
noneC-c C-worg-agenda-refileMove the entry on the agenda's line under another heading, as C-c C-w moves one.
nonesorg-agenda-save-all-buffersSave the buffers of the agenda files (org-agenda-files, and those added to them) with changes not saved, those the agenda changed among them; other Org buffers are left as they are (M-x org-save-all-org-buffers saves them all).
noneC-c C-sorg-agenda-scheduleSchedule the entry on the agenda's line, the date asked for as C-c C-s asks it; with C-u, take its scheduling away.
nonet, C-c C-qorg-agenda-set-tagsSet the tags of the entry on the agenda's line, asked for as C-c C-q asks them.
noneRETorg-agenda-switch-toOpen the entry on the agenda's line in this window, point on its headline.
noneT, C-c T, C-c C-torg-agenda-todoChange the TODO keyword of the entry on the agenda's line to its next, as C-c C-t does in its file: a task done is noted with CLOSED:, one that repeats moves on to its next date.
noneu, C-/, C-_org-agenda-undoUndo the last change made from this agenda, in the file it was made in, and draw the agenda again; when the file was changed there since, nothing is undone and you are told to undo in the file first.
nonew, C-c w, C-x a worg-agenda-week-viewShow the agenda of a week: the week of the day at point in the agenda, else this week.
noneY, C-c Y, C-x a yorg-agenda-year-viewShow the agenda of a year: the year of the day at point in the agenda, else this year.
noneM-x org-align-all-tagsorg-align-all-tagsPut the tags of every headline of the buffer where ORG-TAGS-COLUMN says: by default one space after each one's text, in one step to undo.
noneM-x org-align-tagsorg-align-tagsPut the tags of the headline point is under where ORG-TAGS-COLUMN says: by default one space after its text.

noneM-x org-calendar-backward-monthorg-calendar-backward-monthIn Org's date prompt: the calendar's day a month back, written at the prompt as the same day of the month, or the month's last when it has fewer, as the calendar moves; -1m typed counts on past the month's end instead.
noneM-x org-calendar-backward-weekorg-calendar-backward-weekIn Org's date prompt: the calendar's day a week back, written at the prompt.

noneM-x org-calendar-forward-weekorg-calendar-forward-weekIn Org's date prompt: the calendar's day a week on, written at the prompt.
noneM-x org-calendar-forward-yearorg-calendar-forward-yearIn Org's date prompt: the calendar's day a year on, written at the prompt, so 29 February a year on is 28 February, as the calendar moves; +1y typed is 1 March.
nonea, C-c aorg-calendar-goto-agendaShow the agenda of the week holding the calendar's day at point, point on that day.
noneM-x org-calendar-goto-todayorg-calendar-goto-todayIn Org's date prompt: the calendar on today, written at the prompt.
noneC-c C-x Corg-cancel-taskCancel the task of the headline point is in: its keyword made CANCELLED, a done keyword that M-x org-todo and the other keys that go round the keywords pass over, noted with CLOSED: and when as a task done is.

noneC-c C-corg-capture-finalizeFile the text of this Capture buffer where its template says, and go back to where you were; with its template's clock, clock it.

nonei, C-c iorg-capture-on-dayCapture, as C-x a c does, for the day at point in the calendar or on the agenda (the day of its line, or of the date above it), so that the agenda lists the entry that day: the template's %t and %T are that day's date, and a template with neither gets that date on the line after its heading.

noneC-x a o, C-c C-x C-oorg-clock-outClock out (C-c C-x C-o, from any buffer C-x a o): the clock's line finished with the time it ended and how long it ran; with none running, of the one left open in the agenda files (ORG-CLOCK-RUNNING).

noneM-x org-cycle-list-bulletorg-cycle-list-bulletGive the list point is in its next kind of bullet (C-c -): - to + to * to 1.

nonesrimu-toggle-sortOrder this list by name or by time, those changed last first; the mode line says which.

noneC-M-Vscroll-other-window-downScroll the next window backward by nearly a screenful, leaving the selected one as it is.
noneC-v, <next>scroll-up-commandScroll the window forward by nearly a screenful: by the rows it shows, where long lines wrap.

m CC-z m Cselect-commentSelect the comment around point with the comment lines right before and after it.
m cC-z m cselect-comment-insideSelect the comment around point.
m XC-z m Xselect-elementSelect all of the element around point, its tags too.
m xC-z m xselect-element-insideSelect what is between the tags of the element around point: in HTML, XML, JSX, Svelte and Vue.
m EC-z m Eselect-entrySelect all of the entry around point, its key and value or the list's item.
m eC-z m eselect-entry-insideSelect the key or the value at point of the entry around it: of a key and its value in JSON, YAML or TOML, a field of a struct, an item of a list, as the language's rules know them.
m FC-z m Fselect-functionSelect all of the function around point.
m fC-z m fselect-function-insideSelect the body of the function around point: the block of a Rust fn or closure, the body of a shell function, the forms of a Lisp defun, defmacro, defgeneric, defmethod or lambda after its lambda list.
m iC-z m iselect-inside-pairSelect what is inside a pair of delimiters, the delimiters left out: the pair of the delimiter at point, or the one whose half is typed next ((, ), [, ", ', =, * and the rest of pair-delimiters).
VC-z Vselect-linesStart a line selection anchored on the current line, or cancel a live one.
JC-z Jselect-next-lineMove down, extending the line selection if one is active.
noneM-nselect-next-siblingSelect the next piece of syntax beside the selection, or beside the one at point: the next argument, statement or item, and after the last one, the next beside the piece around them.
m aC-z m aselect-pairSelect a pair of delimiters and what it holds, as select-inside-pair finds it.
m pC-z m pselect-paragraphSelect the paragraph at point with one blank line, the one before it (the one after, for the first paragraph), so that deleting it leaves one blank line between its neighbours: from a blank line between two, the one below.
m PC-z m Pselect-paragraph-backwardSelect the paragraph at point, or grow a paragraph selection backward: from a blank line between two, the one above.
m RC-z m Rselect-parameterSelect the parameter or argument around point with the comma after it.
m rC-z m rselect-parameter-insideSelect the parameter or argument around point: of a Rust function's parameters, a call's arguments or a generic's parameters; of a shell command's arguments; of a Lisp lambda list or a call's arguments.
KC-z Kselect-previous-lineMove up, extending the line selection if one is active.
noneM-pselect-previous-siblingSelect the piece of syntax before the selection, or before the one at point: the argument, statement or item before it, and before the first one, the one before the piece around them.
m sC-z m sselect-sentenceSelect the sentence at point, as far as its full stop; from the gap between two, the one ahead.
m SC-z m Sselect-sentence-backwardSelect the sentence at point, or grow a sentence selection backward: from the gap between two, the one behind.
m AC-z m Aselect-sexpSelect the bracketed expression around point, its brackets included: point at the start, the mark at the end.
m IC-z m Iselect-sexp-insideSelect what is inside the bracketed expression around point, its brackets left out: point at the start, the mark at the end.
m WC-z m Wselect-symbolSelect the symbol at point (a name with its _ and -, Lisp's own characters in Lisp), punctuation at either end left out: from the gap between two, the one ahead, brackets and quotes crossed.
m BC-z m Bselect-symbol-backwardSelect the symbol at point, or grow a symbol selection backward: from the gap between two, the one behind.
m YC-z m Yselect-testSelect all of the test around point.
m yC-z m yselect-test-insideSelect the body of the test around point: a Rust function marked #[test], a Python function whose name begins with test, a Go TestX or BenchmarkX, and the tests of Zig, Elixir, Dart, Julia and others, as the language's rules know them.
m TC-z m Tselect-typeSelect all of the type around point.
m tC-z m tselect-type-insideSelect the body of the type around point: the fields, variants or items of a Rust struct, enum, union, trait or impl; in Lisp, what follows the name in a defclass, defstruct, define-condition or deftype.
%noneselect-whole-bufferSelect the whole buffer: point at the start, the mark at the end.
noneC-M-kselect-window-aboveSelect the window above the selected one: the one over point's column.
noneC-M-jselect-window-belowSelect the window below the selected one: the one under point's column.
noneC-M-hselect-window-leftSelect the window to the left of the selected one: the one beside point's line.
noneC-M-lselect-window-rightSelect the window to the right of the selected one: the one beside point's line.
m wC-z m wselect-wordSelect the word at point; from the gap between two words, the one ahead (the last one at the end of the text).
m bC-z m bselect-word-backwardSelect the word at point, or grow a word selection backward, as select-word grows it forward: from the gap between two words, the one behind.

noneA, C-c Aserver-toggle-agentForward your ssh agent to the server on the line, or those marked, or no longer: on, the programs there can sign with your keys while a client shows its daemon, each use asked about here, and only for the machines named by H where OpenSSH can limit them.
noneC, C-c Cserver-toggle-clipboardShare the clipboard with the server on the line, or those marked, or no longer: on, what is copied there reaches the clipboard here, as text with no control characters, and the daemon there may read what is copied here.
noneF, C-c Fserver-toggle-filesSend the files dropped on a window showing the daemon of the server on the line, or those marked, to a directory there, asked for (from the home directory there unless it begins with /), or no longer: on, a file dropped is copied there, its size checked first, and nothing of it run.
noneG, C-c Gserver-toggle-gpgForward gpg-agent to the server on the line, or those marked, or no longer: on, gpg there signs and decrypts with your keys, which stay here, and cannot export or change them.

noneT, C-c Tserver-tuatara-programName, in the minibuffer, the tuatara to run on the server on the line, or those marked, when it is not the one on the PATH of the commands ssh runs there: /opt/tuatara/bin/tuatara, or a name found on that PATH; empty for the one on that PATH.

noneC-x RET C-\set-input-methodChoose an input method and turn it on in this buffer (C-x RET C-\).

noneC-SPCset-mark-commandSet the mark at point and activate the region (C-SPC).

22.1 Commands that switch to a major mode

A major mode sets how Tuatara treats one kind of text, as chapter 13 describes. Each major mode has a command named after it that switches the current buffer to that mode. Most have no key, because Tuatara picks the mode from the file's name and contents when it opens the file. The commands are listed here, apart from the rest, so that the table above can be read through.
